newsitem.title: USA: CSX, Norfolk up Conrail benefits - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: CSX, Norfolk up Conrail benefits - WSJ.

text.p: CSX Corp and Norfolk Southern Corp now see their breakup of Conrail Inc eventually will reap them more than $800 million a year in savings and gains in operating income, the Wall Street Journal said.

In Monday's electronic edition, the Journal said those projections are 25 percent more than the previous estimates. The revised projections are to be part of a filing with the federal government scheduled to be submitted later today.

In the filing, CSX is expected to increase its estimate of benefits from the Conrail backup to at least $400 million a year from an original estimate of $240 million a year in the third year after the merger, sources told the Journal.
Norfolk Southern is expected to raise its $399 million projection of benefits in the third year, but will offer a more modest increase than CSX.
CSX and Norfolk Southern are expected to submit plans for their proposed purchase of Conrail to federal regulators early this week, sources told Reuters late last week.
The two railroads are seeking to acquire Conrail, an East Coast freight carrier, for $10.3 billion in cash.
